note: Recorded answers for 'Why this step?' when the explainer is off. Written by the team from the cited excerpts; not clinically reviewed (see docs/medical-review.md).

answers.cp-1-ecg: An Earth guideline for suspected heart attack recommends recording an ECG straight away. There is no space-specific guidance for this step.
answers.cp-2-defibrillator-ready: The same Earth guideline says everyone caring for a suspected heart attack should have a defibrillator to hand.
answers.cp-3-restrain: If a shock is needed, the defibrillator may only be used on a patient restrained to an electrically isolated, safe surface, so restrain early.
answers.cp-4-mission-control: The crew must tell Mission Control about an ongoing medical emergency. On a Mars mission the reply is delayed, so the crew does not wait for it.
answers.cp-5-medication: This tool never names a drug or a dose. Any medication is decided by the flight surgeon or the onboard medical checklist.
